name: Ptarmigan Ridge
approach: The road to Mowich Lake is closed indefinitely: WSDOT permanently closed the Fairfax Bridge on SR 165 on April 22, 2025, and the park's road-status page (updated September 18, 2026) lists no public access to Mowich Lake from SR 165, so the White River side is the only start a car can reach. Historically approached either from the west via Mowich Lake (shorter) or from the east via White River Campground (longer, typically requiring a car shuttle or carryover with descent via the Emmons Glacier). Even before the closure, the summer-only Mowich Lake road usually opened well after this route came into condition, so the White River side, with its much longer walk, was often the practical start anyway.

days.note: Hike from White River via Glacier Basin and St. Elmo Pass, across the Winthrop Glacier, Curtis Ridge and the Carbon Glacier toward the base of the ridge, camping partway up.
days.title: Approach to lower camp
days.objective: Cross toward the base of the ridge

days.note: Continue up the ridge to a high bivy around 10,300 ft, with time to melt water, eat, and watch avalanche activity on the surrounding faces before the push.
days.title: Move to high camp

days.note: About 7 hours of technical climbing from high camp to the summit plateau, then tag the summit and descend the Emmons-Winthrop.
days.title: Summit day

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Early, to get a quick start onto the lower ridge

schedule.label: Technical ridge climbing
schedule.detail: ~7 hours from high camp to the summit plateau

days.objective: Climb the technical upper ridge to the summit

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip (~9,500 ft gain): an approach day, a move to the 10,300 ft high camp, then a single summit day with about 7 hours of technical climbing.

waypoints.name: White River Campground
waypoints.directions: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east to the White River Entrance of the park and turn west onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,400 ft; the Glacier Basin Trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Liberty Cap (commonly the route's summit point)
